trick: Trick: 'Icon' means a symbol; they symbolize the software hidden behind them.
tip: Icons visually represent files and applications in Windows.

question: If you want to close an unresponsive application window directly without using the mouse, which keyboard shortcut should you use?
explanation: Step 1: Identify the active window you want to close. Step 2: Pressing Alt + F4 sends a close command directly to that program. Use Case: Rapidly closing multiple open PDF files at the end of the workday.
trick: Trick: 'Alt + F4' shuts the door (closes the app).
tip: Use Alt + F4 to close the currently active window.

question: Which of the following is the most current and modern version of the Windows Operating System available today?
explanation: Step 1: Track Microsoft's latest releases. Step 2: Windows 11 was released in 2021 as the successor to Windows 10, bringing a centered taskbar and new design. Use Case: Buying a brand-new laptop today will typically come with Windows 11.
trick: Trick: 11 is the highest and latest number in the Windows series.
tip: Windows 11 is the latest major operating system version.

question: What is the primary function of the 'Start Menu' in the Windows environment?
options: To search for apps, access settings, and shut down the PC
To write and execute programming code
answer: To search for apps, access settings, and shut down the PC
explanation: Step 1: The Start Menu is the central hub of Windows. Step 2: It provides access to installed programs, system settings, and power options. Use Case: Clicking Start to find the 'Calculator' app or to restart the computer.
trick: Trick: Everything you need to 'Start' doing on your PC is in this menu.
tip: The Start Menu is the central navigation hub.

question: Ravi copied a paragraph from Wikipedia using 'Ctrl + C'. Which shortcut must he use to place that text into his Word document?
explanation: Step 1: 'Ctrl + C' stores the text in the clipboard. Step 2: 'Ctrl + V' is the shortcut to paste the stored text into the new location. Use Case: Pasting an OTP code copied from an email into a banking website.
trick: Trick: The 'V' looks like an arrowhead pointing down, pasting the text into place.
tip: Ctrl + V is the standard shortcut to paste.

question: Fill in the blank: The main screen area that you see after you turn on your computer and log in to Windows is called the ____.
explanation: Step 1: The primary workspace appears after the boot process. Step 2: This area, which holds your wallpaper and icons, is named the Desktop. Use Case: Saving a temporary file to the Desktop for easy access later.
trick: Trick: Just like a physical desk, you place your working materials on top of it.
tip: The Desktop is your primary visual workspace in Windows.

question: What is the difference between 'Cut' (Ctrl + X) and 'Copy' (Ctrl + C) in Windows file management?
options: Cut leaves the original file; Copy deletes it
Cut deletes the file permanently; Copy moves it
Cut moves the file to a new location; Copy creates a duplicate
answer: Cut moves the file to a new location; Copy creates a duplicate
explanation: Step 1: 'Copy' duplicates data, leaving the original intact. Step 2: 'Cut' removes the original data once it is pasted elsewhere. Use Case: Cutting a photo from the Downloads folder to organize it into the Pictures folder.
trick: Trick: 'Cut' acts like scissors, cutting it out of its original place.
tip: Cut moves data; Copy duplicates data.

question: Which Windows 10/11 shortcut lets you quickly lock your computer when you step away from your desk?
explanation: Step 1: Leaving a PC unlocked in an office is a security risk. Step 2: Pressing Win + L instantly brings up the lock screen, requiring a password to re-enter. Use Case: Securing a bank teller system during a lunch break.
trick: Trick: 'L' stands for Lock.
tip: Use Windows Key + L to instantly lock your PC.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major version of the Windows Operating System?
explanation: Step 1: Review the release history: XP, Vista, 7, 8, 10, 11. Step 2: Microsoft entirely skipped the number 9. Use Case: Identifying fake software downloads that claim to be 'Windows 9'.
trick: Trick: 7, 8, 10. Number 9 does not exist in the Windows universe.
tip: There is no operating system named Windows 9.

question: If Neha accidentally deletes a paragraph in her Word document, which shortcut can she use to 'Undo' her mistake?
explanation: Step 1: Mistakes happen frequently during typing or file movement. Step 2: 'Ctrl + Z' is the universal undo command in Windows to reverse the last action. Use Case: Bringing back a mistakenly deleted folder on the desktop.
trick: Trick: 'Z' is the last letter, taking you back one step in time.
tip: Ctrl + Z undoes your last action.

question: Fill in the blank: The area at the far right of the Taskbar that displays the system clock, volume icon, and network status is called the ____.
explanation: Step 1: Look at the bottom right corner of the screen. Step 2: This area holds background system icons and notifications, known as the System Tray. Use Case: Clicking the Wi-Fi icon in the System Tray to connect to a network.
trick: Trick: It holds a 'tray' of tiny system icons.
tip: The System Tray shows background tasks and the clock.

question: In Windows, what does it mean to 'Pin' an application to the Taskbar?
options: It forces the application to close
It creates a permanent shortcut icon on the taskbar for quick access
It stops the application from using the internet
answer: It creates a permanent shortcut icon on the taskbar for quick access
explanation: Step 1: Usually, app icons disappear from the taskbar when closed. Step 2: Pinning locks the icon there, even when closed, acting as a quick-launch button. Use Case: Pinning Google Chrome to the taskbar because you use it daily.
trick: Trick: You physically 'pin' it to the bar so it doesn't fall away.
tip: Pinning creates a quick-access shortcut on the taskbar.

question: Which of these keyboard shortcuts opens the 'File Explorer' (My Computer/This PC) to browse your hard drive?
explanation: Step 1: Users frequently need to browse folders. Step 2: Pressing Win + E instantly opens a new File Explorer window. Use Case: Quickly opening Explorer to find a PDF saved in the Downloads folder.
trick: Trick: 'E' stands for Explorer.
tip: Win + E is the quickest way to open File Explorer.

question: What is the classic keyboard shortcut to open the 'Task Manager', often used when a computer program is frozen and needs to be force-closed?
explanation: Step 1: When a PC freezes, standard clicks won't work. Step 2: The hardware interrupt 'Ctrl + Alt + Delete' opens a security screen where Task Manager can be launched to kill the frozen app. Use Case: Forcing a crashed video game to close.
trick: Trick: The famous 'Three-finger salute' saves a stuck PC.
tip: Ctrl + Alt + Delete helps recover a frozen computer.

question: Fill in the blank: If you right-click on an empty space on the Windows desktop, a ____ menu appears, giving options like View, Sort by, and Refresh.
explanation: Step 1: Right-clicking brings up a list of actions. Step 2: Because these actions change depending on what you click (desktop vs. a file), it is called a Context Menu. Use Case: Right-clicking the desktop to select 'New Folder'.
trick: Trick: The menu changes based on the 'context' of your click.
tip: Right-clicking opens a context-sensitive popup menu.

question: When referring to Windows GUI, what are the three standard window control buttons found in the top-right corner of almost every application?
explanation: Step 1: Look at the top right of any window (like Notepad). Step 2: You will see a dash (Minimize), a square (Maximize), and an X (Close). Use Case: Clicking the dash to temporarily hide a calculator window.
trick: Trick: Dash, Box, Cross = Hide, Grow, Kill.
tip: The top-right corner houses Minimize, Maximize, and Close buttons.

question: Which of the following versions of Windows is famous for having the default 'Bliss' wallpaper, featuring bright rolling green hills and a blue sky?
explanation: Step 1: Identify classic Windows imagery. Step 2: The 'Bliss' photo is iconic and served as the default desktop background for the highly popular Windows XP. Use Case: Recognizing legacy systems still running in older government offices.
trick: Trick: XP stands for eXtra Peaceful (like those green hills).
tip: Windows XP featured the famous green hills Bliss wallpaper.

question: What is the function of the 'Windows Key + R' shortcut?
options: It opens the Run dialog box to execute commands
answer: It opens the Run dialog box to execute commands
explanation: Step 1: Power users often want to open apps by typing their names. Step 2: Win + R opens the 'Run' box at the bottom left. Use Case: Pressing Win + R and typing 'cmd' to open the Command Prompt quickly.
trick: Trick: 'R' stands for Run.
tip: Win + R quickly opens the Run command box.

question: Fill in the blank: To rapidly switch between multiple open applications (like Word and Excel) without touching the mouse, hold down the 'Alt' key and press ____.
explanation: Step 1: Multitasking requires fast switching. Step 2: 'Alt + Tab' brings up a visual switcher overlay; tapping Tab cycles through the open windows. Use Case: Copying data from a PDF and instantly Alt+Tabbing to paste it in Word.
trick: Trick: 'Tab' through your alternate (Alt) applications.
tip: Alt + Tab switches between active open windows.

question: By default, which application acts as the built-in web browser in Windows 10 and Windows 11?
explanation: Step 1: Internet Explorer is obsolete. Step 2: Microsoft replaced it with Edge as the default pre-installed browser in Win 10 and 11. Use Case: Using Edge to download Chrome on a brand new laptop.
trick: Trick: It gives Windows users an 'Edge' on the internet.
tip: Microsoft Edge is the default modern Windows browser.

question: What does the keyboard shortcut 'Ctrl + A' do when you are inside a folder containing 50 photos?
options: It selects all the photos at once
It copies the photos to a pen drive
answer: It selects all the photos at once
explanation: Step 1: Clicking 50 files individually is slow. Step 2: 'Ctrl + A' selects 'All' items in the active window simultaneously. Use Case: Selecting an entire album of photos to drag them into a backup folder.
trick: Trick: 'A' stands for Select All.
tip: Ctrl + A selects everything in the current view.

question: Which visual GUI change was heavily promoted in Windows 11 compared to Windows 10?
options: The Start Menu and Taskbar icons were moved to the center of the screen
The Taskbar was permanently moved to the top
Icons were replaced by text commands
answer: The Start Menu and Taskbar icons were moved to the center of the screen
explanation: Step 1: For decades, the Start button was on the bottom left. Step 2: Windows 11 modernized the look by centering the Start button and app icons on the Taskbar. Use Case: Recognizing a Windows 11 PC just by looking at the centered taskbar.
trick: Trick: Win 11 is 'centered' on modern design.
tip: Windows 11 features a centered Start button and taskbar.

question: Fill in the blank: The topmost area of an open window (like Notepad) that displays the name of the file currently open is called the ____.
explanation: Step 1: Look at the top edge of any application. Step 2: It shows the 'Title' of the document, making it the Title Bar. Use Case: Clicking and dragging the Title Bar to move the window across the monitor.
trick: Trick: It holds the 'Title' of your work.
tip: The Title Bar displays the active document's name.

question: If you want to quickly open the Windows 'Settings' menu to connect a Bluetooth mouse, which shortcut is the fastest?
explanation: Step 1: Going through the Start menu takes multiple clicks. Step 2: Pressing Win + I opens the main Settings panel instantly. Use Case: Quickly checking your Wi-Fi network properties.
trick: Trick: 'I' stands for Information/Settings.
tip: Win + I instantly opens the Windows Settings menu.

question: Which of these old Windows tools has Microsoft been slowly replacing with the modern 'Settings' app in Windows 10 and 11?
explanation: Step 1: Historically, PC changes were made in the Control Panel. Step 2: To make Windows touch-friendly, Microsoft created 'Settings' and is phasing out the Control Panel. Use Case: Changing the desktop wallpaper via Settings instead of the old Control Panel.
trick: Trick: The old 'Panel' is retiring for modern 'Settings'.
tip: The Control Panel is slowly being replaced by Settings.

question: How can you restore a file that you accidentally sent to the Recycle Bin?
options: Right-click the file inside the Recycle Bin and choose 'Restore'
Double-click the file and click Save
answer: Right-click the file inside the Recycle Bin and choose 'Restore'
explanation: Step 1: Open the Recycle Bin. Step 2: Right-clicking the deleted file gives the 'Restore' option, sending it back to its original folder. Use Case: Bringing back a wrongly deleted Excel sheet for the boss.
trick: Trick: 'Restore' restores it to its original glory.
tip: Use the 'Restore' option to recover deleted files.

question: Fill in the blank: When you copy a piece of text, it is temporarily stored in an invisible memory area called the ____ until you paste it.
explanation: Step 1: Data needs a holding area between Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V. Step 2: Windows uses a virtual space in RAM called the Clipboard. Use Case: Copying an address from a website and pasting it into an email.
trick: Trick: Like a real clipboard holding a paper until you need it.
tip: The Clipboard temporarily holds copied or cut data.

question: What is the primary purpose of the 'Snipping Tool' (or Snip & Sketch) built into Windows?
options: To take custom screenshots of specific parts of the screen
answer: To take custom screenshots of specific parts of the screen
explanation: Step 1: 'Print Screen' captures the whole monitor. Step 2: The Snipping tool lets you drag a box to capture just a small error message or image. Use Case: Taking a picture of a transaction ID to send to a friend.
trick: Trick: 'Snip' means to cut out a small visual piece of the screen.
tip: Snipping Tool is used for taking custom screenshots.

question: In the Windows file system, what letter is almost always assigned to the primary hard drive partition where the Windows OS itself is installed?
explanation: Step 1: Early PCs reserved A: and B: for floppy disk drives. Step 2: The first hard drive was assigned C:, and this convention remains today for the primary OS drive. Use Case: Navigating to C:\Program Files to find installed software.
trick: Trick: 'C' is the Core drive of your computer.
tip: The primary OS drive is universally designated as C:.

question: Which key do you press in combination with 'Windows Key' to quickly connect to a projector or an external monitor?
explanation: Step 1: Connecting external displays requires choosing how to show the screen (Duplicate, Extend). Step 2: Win + P opens the Project menu instantly. Use Case: Connecting a laptop to an office projector for a PowerPoint presentation.
trick: Trick: 'P' stands for Projector or Project.
tip: Win + P opens external display/projector settings.

question: Fill in the blank: The classic built-in Windows application used for completely basic text editing, writing code, and stripping away text formatting (like bold or italics) is called ____.
explanation: Step 1: Word processors add hidden formatting data. Step 2: Notepad is pure plain text, making it perfect for raw notes or coding scripts. Use Case: Removing weird font formatting from a website text by pasting it into Notepad first.
trick: Trick: It is literally just a plain pad for notes.
tip: Notepad is a basic, formatting-free text editor.

question: What happens when you double-click the Title Bar (the top strip) of an open window that is currently taking up half the screen?
options: The window maximizes to fill the entire screen
The window minimizes to the Taskbar
answer: The window maximizes to fill the entire screen
explanation: Step 1: Hitting the small square 'maximize' button requires precision. Step 2: Double-clicking anywhere on the wide Title Bar achieves the same maximization quickly. Use Case: Rapidly expanding a small browser window to read a long article.
trick: Trick: Double-clicking the top 'blows up' the window to full size.
tip: Double-click the Title Bar to maximize a window.

question: Which of these is the default digital voice assistant integrated into Windows 10 by Microsoft?
explanation: Step 1: Apple has Siri, Amazon has Alexa. Step 2: Microsoft integrated Cortana (named after an AI in the game Halo) into the Windows Taskbar. Use Case: Using your microphone to ask the PC, 'What is the weather today?'
trick: Trick: Cortana is the Windows assistant.
tip: Cortana is Microsoft's built-in digital voice assistant.

question: If you want to search for a specific file or setting on your Windows 10 computer, where is the most direct place to type your query?
options: The Search Box on the Taskbar (next to Start)
answer: The Search Box on the Taskbar (next to Start)
explanation: Step 1: Finding files manually is slow. Step 2: The Search Box (or magnifying glass icon) next to the Start button searches the entire PC and web instantly. Use Case: Typing 'Bluetooth' in the Search Box to quickly find Bluetooth settings.
trick: Trick: It is a box meant for searching, sitting right next to Start.
tip: Use the Taskbar Search Box to find files/settings.

question: Fill in the blank: To quickly create a completely 'New Folder' on your desktop without right-clicking, you can use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + ____ + N.
explanation: Step 1: 'Ctrl + N' usually opens a new file or window. Step 2: Adding 'Shift' (Ctrl + Shift + N) explicitly tells Windows to create a New Folder. Use Case: Quickly organizing a messy desktop into named folders.
trick: Trick: 'Shift' to a New Folder instead of a new file.
tip: Ctrl + Shift + N instantly creates a new folder.

question: In the Task Manager, which specific tab should you check to see which applications are automatically launching the moment you turn on your computer?
explanation: Step 1: Some apps (like Antivirus or Skype) boot with Windows, slowing it down. Step 2: The 'Startup' tab lists these and lets you disable them. Use Case: Disabling Spotify from opening by itself every time you log in.
trick: Trick: Programs here 'start up' when the PC 'starts up'.
tip: The Startup tab controls apps that launch automatically.

question: Which of the following is an example of an Operating System that is completely text-based (Command Line Interface) and is the ancestor of modern Windows?
explanation: Step 1: Before GUI, computers used text commands. Step 2: Microsoft's original OS was MS-DOS (Microsoft Disk Operating System). Use Case: The modern 'Command Prompt' app in Windows simulates this old MS-DOS environment.
trick: Trick: DOS stands for Disk Operating System (the text-based grandpa of Windows).
tip: MS-DOS was Microsoft's original text-based operating system.

question: What is the function of the 'Action Center' icon located at the far right of the Windows 10 Taskbar?
options: It shows system notifications and quick toggle buttons (like Wi-Fi/Bluetooth)
It acts as a video player
answer: It shows system notifications and quick toggle buttons (like Wi-Fi/Bluetooth)
explanation: Step 1: Users need a central place for alerts and quick settings, similar to a smartphone dropdown. Step 2: The Action Center groups emails, system alerts, and toggle buttons. Use Case: Clicking the Action Center to quickly turn on 'Airplane Mode'.
trick: Trick: It is the center where you take 'Action' on notifications.
tip: Action Center houses notifications and quick settings.

question: Fill in the blank: The 'Aero Snap' feature in Windows allows you to easily multitask by dragging a window to the left or right edge of the screen, which automatically snaps it to fill exactly ____ of the screen.
explanation: Step 1: Working with two apps simultaneously is common. Step 2: Dragging a window to the screen edge 'snaps' it to fill exactly 50% (half) of the monitor. Use Case: Snapping a web browser to the left half and MS Word to the right half to take notes.
trick: Trick: It snaps the screen cleanly in two halves.
tip: Aero Snap automatically sizes windows to half the screen.
